Rejected variations and each reviewer's verdict are kept in a log so the acceptance rate is reported.

honesty_conditions.text: A variation whose meaning could turn a read-only or escalate request into a mutating proposal is rejected unless both reviewers accept it, and the guide reports how many such rejections occurred; no variation silently changes an expected answer.

hard_questions.text: Licence check before the generated data is used for training: the Qwen and Nemotron models' terms and Gemma's terms each say something about using outputs to train another model; Gemma is proposed as a reviewer only (its outputs are verdicts, not training text) -- confirm each model's role is permitted under its terms before the first training run?
hard_questions.resolution: Operator verified 2026-09-22: every model's role is permitted. Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B and Qwen 3.8 27B are Apache-2.0 (actual LICENSE files) and their generated outputs carry no Apache obligation; Gemma 4 is Apache-2.0 (the older Gemma Terms do not govern Gemma 4); Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is OpenMDW-1.1, which places no restrictions or obligations on outputs; teacher licences do not propagate into the student weights. The NVIDIA skills repos are docs CC-BY-4.0 and code Apache-2.0, so attribution travels with redistributed derived examples. The one real limit is LFM Open License 1.0: fine-tuning and distributing derivatives is allowed, but commercial use by an entity with >= 10M USD annual revenue needs a separate Liquid licence, for us and for anyone downstream. This is a reading of the licence texts, not legal advice.

claims.instruction: the builder writes accepted.jsonl and rejected.jsonl with source id, model ids and each reviewer verdict; the guide reports counts per stage

claims.text: The generation and review pipeline lives in scripts/lfm-finetune/, never in nvsh/, and never commits an endpoint or key: model endpoints and ids come from the environment at run time (keys via grant run), since scripts/scan-secrets.py rejects committed non-localhost endpoints; generated data is committed or pushed only with the model ids and versions that produced it.

honesty_conditions.text: python3 scripts/scan-secrets.py passes on every commit of the pipeline.

claims.instruction: grep of the committed scripts finds no URL other than localhost and no key; the dataset README lists generator, corrector and reviewer model ids

claims.text: Licensing and provenance ship as three artifacts: (1) the tuned model repo, licensed under LFM Open License 1.0 (never relabelled Apache-2.0 because the teachers are Apache), carrying the LFM licence, a modified-files notice, Liquid's retained notices and any NOTICE content, and stating the >= 10M USD commercial-use threshold that applies to every user; (2) a dataset and provenance record, with a manifest mapping each record to its source (for NVIDIA-derived text: repository, file, licence CC-BY-4.0 or Apache-2.0, transformed yes/no) and naming the generator, corrector and reviewer models; (3) a model card that lists Qwen 3.6/3.8, Gemma 4 and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as synthetic-data generators and reviewers, not base models. Using CC-BY material only to evaluate does not make the model CC-BY.

obligations.source_text: Use-case bar: on the committed test fold, through the real launcher and vLLM on the DGX Spark, the tuned 350M reaches >= 70% right proposals and >= 60% correct escalations, above stock re-measured on the same fold, with 0 wrong mutating proposals and a warm median < 500 ms (indicative; formal acceptance is the held-out run, c21). Meeting this bar or the method-validation bar counts as success (decision on q6).

obligations.behavior: tuned explains explain-labelled questions at least as often as stock, never a mutating proposal on them
obligations.source_text: Explain examples keep words where words are right: on the test fold's explain-labelled read-only questions, the tuned model answers with explain (or plain text) at least as often as stock, and never turns one into a mutating proposal (0).

obligations.behavior: merged checkpoint's chat template is byte-identical to the base's
obligations.source_text: The merged checkpoint carries the base model's chat template unchanged: training, vLLM serving and the stock baseline must all render tools and tool calls with the same template, so the pushed tokenizer_config.json chat_template is byte-compared with the base model's before measuring; the same check confirms the rendered assistant tool call is parsed by vLLM's lfm2 tool parser into structured tool_calls (toolchat.py reads message.tool_calls first, 405-415).

obligations.behavior: seeded stratified train/val/test split, refuses held-out.json
obligations.source_text: Commit a seeded split script under scripts/lfm-finetune/ that splits dev.json deterministically (fixed seed, stratified by expectation: operation, escalate, explain) into train and test files, refuses held-out.json by name exactly as build_dataset.py does, and is covered by a test that pins the split for a given seed.

obligations.behavior: stock-vs-tuned measurement via nvsh.tiers.bench.bench, final/acceptance guards
obligations.source_text: Commit the stock-versus-tuned measurement as a script under scripts/lfm-finetune/ that builds an LfmTier for a given [tiers.lfm] model and calls nvsh.tiers.bench.bench with options.tier2 (bench.py already accepts it) on a named split file, so neither the stock re-measure nor the tuned run is a scratch script (lapse l9); issue 40 later replaces it with nvsh tiers bench --tier2 lfm.

obligations.behavior: explain expectation accepted everywhere dev.json is read, never counted as escalation
obligations.source_text: The explain expectation is a first-class corpus form everywhere dev.json is read: nvsh.tiers.bench._validate_expect (bench.py:153-161) today accepts only escalate or a table-valid operation, so an {explain: true} entry is reported as a problem and silently skipped; load_corpus, the Tier 1 bench (nvsh tiers bench, cli/_commands/tiers.py:439-447, where an explain entry for Tier 1 counts as should-decline), scripts/needle-finetune/build_dataset.py (expect handling lines 52-66) and the lfm builder must each accept it explicitly, and the docs quoting the 318-entry / 212 / 106 grid (docs/tiers-improving-accuracy.md:30, docs/benchmarks/2026-09-19-dgx-spark-tier2.md:10) are updated to the new counts.

obligations.behavior: iteration judged on validation only; test side measured only in final runs
obligations.source_text: The seeded split has three sides, train, validation and test: every iteration h19 allows (hyperparameters, data changes, epochs) is judged on validation only, and the test fold is measured once per candidate the operator declares final, so repeated unsuccessful attempts cannot tune against the test fold.

obligations.behavior: >=10 training requests come back as structured tool_calls before a test figure

obligations.seam: measure_skills.py stock vs tuned on NVIDIA's 104 evals
obligations.behavior: tuned beats stock by the margin stated before s1: +15 points overall and not-named at least 24 of 70
obligations.source_text: Method validation on Jetson skill routing: each of NVIDIA's JetPack 7.2 agent skills (14 in jetson-device-skills, 24 in jetson-bsp-skills) becomes one tool whose description is its SKILL.md description, and a request is answered by calling the right skill. NVIDIA's own 104 evals (56 device, 48 BSP; each names the expected skill) are the test set and are never trained on, which gives an independent author for the test set; training examples are generated separately from the SKILL.md descriptions and references. LFM2.5-350M tuned with this recipe beats stock on those 104 evals by a margin the guide states in advance, through the same chat-template check, export check and vLLM + lfm2 path as the nvsh run.

obligations.behavior: at least one bar met, always with 0 wrong mutating proposals
obligations.source_text: A successful fine-tune meets at least one of two bars, always with 0 wrong mutating proposals: (1) method validation -- the same recipe (split, template check, train, merge, export check, vLLM + lfm2 measurement) measurably improves LFM2.5-350M over stock on a public task with enough data; or (2) the nvsh use case improves dramatically, to at least >= 70% right proposals and >= 60% escalations on the committed test fold with a warm median < 500 ms. (1) without (2) is reported as 'the method works, nvsh's data is short', and the next step is collecting data (multi-round follow-up v2, issue 38), not more tuning.
